1. INTRODUCTION

The Meridian County Heritage Trust (MCHT) presents its Annual Budget and Operational Plan for Fiscal Year 2025 (FY2025), covering the period from 2025-07-01 through 2026-06-30. This document consolidates the institutional budget, departmental allocations, and key operational priorities for the coming year. It serves as the primary financial and planning reference for all MCHT staff, the Board of Trustees, and our funding partners.

This plan reflects the Trust’s continued commitment to responsible stewardship of the county’s cultural heritage, balanced growth of our public programs, and the preservation of our collections for future generations. The budget and operational priorities outlined herein were developed through a collaborative process involving department heads, the Finance Office, and the Board’s Finance Committee, with final adoption occurring at the regular Board meeting on 2025-04-10.

2. TOTAL ANNUAL BUDGET

The Meridian County Heritage Trust annual_budget for the current fiscal year is 1250000 USD. Record status: current. This figure represents a 4.2% increase over the FY2024 adopted budget of $1,200,000 and reflects additional revenue from increased county appropriations, expanded membership, and a successful capital campaign for the East Wing renovation, completed in late 2024.

This total annual budget is the baseline for all departmental allocations and expenditure plans detailed in Section 3 below. All financial reporting and variance analysis for FY2025 will be measured against this adopted budget figure.

The Collections & Conservation department receives the largest single allocation in FY2025, reflecting the Trust’s recognition that the care and preservation of our collections is the foundation of all our work. Key priorities for this department in FY2025 include:

**6.1 Collections Stewardship Policy Overview**

The Meridian County Heritage Trust (MCHT) is committed to the responsible stewardship of the collections held in the public trust. This Section establishes the operational framework for the care, documentation, access, and preservation of all objects, specimens, and archival materials in the permanent collection, as well as long-term loans. The policy is reviewed annually by the Collections Committee and the Board of Trustees.

The stewardship program is guided by the following core principles:

- **Preventive Conservation:** Maintaining stable environmental conditions and implementing integrated pest management to prevent damage.
- **Documentation:** Maintaining accurate, complete, and accessible records for every object, from acquisition through deaccession.
- **Access:** Balancing public and scholarly access with the long-term preservation needs of the collection.
- **Professional Standards:** Adhering to the codes of ethics and best practices established by the American Alliance of Museums and the American Institute for Conservation.

**6.2 Collections Committee**

The Collections Committee is a standing committee of the Board of Trustees responsible for reviewing and making recommendations on acquisitions, deaccessions, loans, and other collection-related matters. The Committee meets at least quarterly and as needed for urgent matters.

#### 7.2 Work Order System

All maintenance and repair requests shall be submitted through the Facilities Work Order System (FWOS). The system is administered by the Facilities Manager and is accessible to all department heads and authorized staff.

| Priority | Definition | Response Time | Completion Target |

1. **Submission:** Requester completes Form F-201 (Work Order Request) via the FWOS portal or paper form at the Facilities Office.

5. **Documentation:** Completed work orders are closed with a record of actions taken, materials used, and hours billed.

#### 7.5 Conservation and Treatment Protocols

The Conservation Department operates under the supervision of the Chief Conservator and in accordance with the MCHT Collections Management Policy and the Code of Ethics of the American Institute for Conservation. All conservation work, whether performed in-house or by approved external contractors, shall be planned, documented, and reviewed as set forth in this Section.

**7.5.1 Treatment Authorization Levels**

The following authorization levels shall apply to all conservation treatments, including examination, preventive conservation, and interventive treatment:

| Level | Description | Authorizing Authority |
|-------|-------------|----------------------|
| Level I | Examination and documentation only; no physical alteration | Conservator (staff) |
| Level II | Low-risk preventive conservation (e.g., rehousing, mounting, surface cleaning with documented low risk) | Conservator with notice to Registrar |
| Level III | Interventive treatment with minimal risk (e.g., consolidation, inpainting, lining) | Chief Conservator |
| Level IV | Major or high-risk treatment (e.g., structural treatment, extensive loss compensation, treatment of objects on loan) | Chief Conservator and Registrar; Director of Collections notified |
| Level V | Emergency stabilization of an object in imminent danger | Senior Conservator on call; retrospective approval by Chief Conservator within five (5) business days |

No treatment shall begin without a written condition assessment and a signed treatment proposal. For Level III and above, the written proposal must include a justification of the proposed materials and methods, a risk assessment, and a projected schedule and cost estimate. The Registrar shall be notified of all Level III and above treatments prior to commencement.

**7.5.2 Condition Assessments and Treatment Documentation**

A condition assessment shall be completed for every object before it is considered for loan, before it is placed on permanent or temporary display, and upon its return from a loan or exhibition. Assessments shall be recorded on the standard MCHT Condition Report form (Form CR-1) and shall include a written description of the object's condition, a photographic record, and a sketch or diagram where appropriate. A copy of each condition report shall be filed in the object's permanent record in the Collections Management System (CMS) and the original filed with the Registrar.

Treatment documentation shall include the following:

1. **Treatment Proposal:** A written plan of the proposed treatment, including materials, methods, and a schedule.
2. **Treatment Record:** A written narrative of the treatment actually performed, including materials used, methods employed, and any deviations from the proposal.
3. **Photographic Documentation:** Before, during, and after photographs of the treatment, taken under standard lighting conditions and filed with the treatment record.
4. **Final Report:** A summary of the treatment, including an assessment of the outcome and any recommendations for future care.

All treatment documentation shall be reviewed by the Chief Conservator and filed in the object's permanent record.

**7.5.3 Conservation Laboratory Access and Use**

The Conservation Lab shall be accessible only to authorized Conservation Department staff and approved interns, fellows, and contractors. Access to the lab shall be controlled by the Security Department and recorded in the lab access log. All lab users shall complete a safety orientation before working in the lab. Use of lab equipment shall be in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and the lab's standard operating procedures. The Chief Conservator shall maintain an inventory of lab equipment and hazardous materials, and shall review the inventory quarterly.

**8.0 PHOTOGRAPHY AND DOCUMENTATION STANDARDS**

**8.1 Purpose**

This section establishes uniform standards for the creation, handling, and storage of photographic and audiovisual documentation produced by or on behalf of the Trust. These standards apply to all staff, volunteers, interns, fellows, contractors, and visiting researchers. The goal is to ensure that all visual records are accurate, reproducible, and securely preserved as part of the Trust’s permanent institutional memory.

**8.2 Photography Studio Operations**

The Photography Studio, located in the lower level of the Heritage Center (Room B-14), is the primary facility for all controlled photographic work on collection objects. The Studio is equipped with copy stands, light tents, strobes, and a calibrated EIZO monitor for color review. The Studio is scheduled through the Collections Department’s shared calendar; all shoots must be booked at least 48 hours in advance, except for emergency documentation required by the Registrar or Chief Conservator.

Studio access is restricted to authorized staff and approved contractors. A log of all studio sessions shall be maintained by the Photographer, recording the date, object accession number, photographer’s initials, and purpose of the shoot. The log is reviewed monthly by the Registrar.

**8.3 Photography Survey Logs**

The Trust maintains a series of survey logs to track photographic coverage of the permanent collection. The primary log, the **Photography Survey Log (Form PS-1)**, is a master index of all objects photographed since the 1987 inventory. Each entry includes the accession number, object name, date of photography, photographer’s initials, and the location of the digital files. The log is updated within five working days of any new shoot.

A second log, the **Survey Completion Log (Form PS-2)**, tracks the progress of the ongoing effort to photograph the entire collection. As of the start of FY2025, the Trust has complete photographic coverage of 8,412 of the 9,108 objects in the permanent collection. The remaining 696 objects are scheduled for photography over the next two fiscal years, with priority given to objects on loan, objects slated for exhibition, and objects in the Archaeology Collection that have not been photographed since 1995.

**8.4 Digital File Standards**

All born-digital images shall be captured in RAW format and archived as uncompressed TIFF masters. Delivery files for web and publication use shall be JPEG or PNG, generated from the master file. The following naming convention shall be used for all digital files:

*Accession Number_Object Name_View_Date_Photographer Initials*

Example: `1987.004.002_Basin_Overall_20240910_JAB.tif`

All master files shall be stored on the Trust’s network-attached storage (NAS) in the folder structure maintained by the IT Department. A second copy shall be stored on the off-site backup server, which is tested quarterly by IT. No master files shall be stored solely on local drives or removable media.

**8.5 Rights and Reproduction**

The Trust retains all rights to images produced by its staff and contractors during the course of their work. Images of collection objects may be used for internal documentation, conservation, research, and educational purposes without further approval. Any external use, including publication, exhibition, or commercial licensing, requires written approval from the Registrar and, where applicable, the donor or lender.

**Section 9: Collections Management**

**9.1 Scope and Authority**

This section governs the day-to-day care, documentation, movement, and use of the permanent collection and any objects on loan to the Trust. The Registrar is the designated authority for all matters concerning object location, custody, and legal status. Department heads shall ensure that all staff and volunteers under their supervision are familiar with the policies in this section.

**9.2 Accessioning and Deaccessioning**

The Trust shall accession objects into the permanent collection only through the procedures outlined in the Collections Management Policy, approved by the Board of Trustees. No object shall be formally accessioned without a fully executed deed of gift or purchase invoice, a signed receipt from the Registrar, and a preliminary condition report.

Deaccessioning of any object shall follow the same policy, which requires a written recommendation from the Curator of Collections, review by the Collections Committee, and final approval by the Board of Trustees. All deaccession proceeds shall be used exclusively for the acquisition or conservation of collection objects. No deaccession shall occur for the purpose of raising operating funds.

**9.3 Loan Management**

All incoming and outgoing loans shall be administered through the Registrar’s Office. No loan shall be accepted or initiated without a fully executed loan agreement approved by the Registrar and, for outgoing loans, the Director.

| Loan Type | Approval Authority | Agreement Required | Insurance Responsibility |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Incoming (short-term, under 1 year) | Registrar | Yes – Standard Incoming Loan Agreement | Lender, unless otherwise specified |
| Incoming (long-term, 1 year or more) | Director | Yes – Extended Loan Agreement | Trust, at replacement value |
| Outgoing | Director and Curator of Collections | Yes – Standard Outgoing Loan Agreement | Borrowing institution, wall-to-wall |
| Internal (between Trust buildings) | Registrar | No – Internal Movement Form (Form CM-4) | N/A |

The Registrar shall maintain a central loan file for each active loan, containing the signed agreement, condition reports, insurance certificates, correspondence, and a copy of the courier report (if applicable). Loan files shall be reviewed annually for renewal or termination status.

For outgoing loans, the borrowing institution must provide a facilities report that meets the Trust’s environmental and security standards. The Registrar shall verify that the borrower’s insurance certificate names the Trust as an additional insured. A condition report shall be completed by a Trust staff member before shipment and again upon the object’s return.

**9.4 Location Control and Movement**

The Registrar maintains the central location index for all collection objects. Any change in an object’s location shall be reported to the Registrar’s Office within two working days. Departmental staff are responsible for updating the location field in the collections database (TMS) when they move an object within their assigned storage or exhibition areas.

All movement of collection objects within the Trust’s buildings shall be performed by trained staff or authorized volunteers. Objects shall be transported on padded carts or in appropriate crates, and no object shall be left unattended in a corridor or common area.

**9.5 Object Handling**

Only staff who have completed the Trust’s Object Handling Training shall handle collection objects. The training is coordinated by the Curator of Collections and is offered quarterly. A roster of trained staff is maintained by the Registrar’s Office.

**SECTION 10. EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS AND COLLECTION RISK MANAGEMENT**

**10.1 Policy Statement**

The Trust maintains a comprehensive Emergency Preparedness Plan (EPP), current as of March 2024, which addresses fire, flood, severe weather, utility failure, and security incidents affecting any Trust-owned or Trust-operated facility. The EPP is a living document, reviewed annually by the Emergency Preparedness Committee and updated whenever a drill, incident, or facilities assessment identifies a gap. The plan is distributed to all department heads, the Facilities Manager, and the Registrar’s Office; a copy is kept in the Security Office and in the Director’s office.

**10.2 Emergency Preparedness Committee**

The Committee is chaired by the Facilities Manager and includes the Curator of Collections, the Registrar, the Head of Security, and the Director of Administration. The Committee meets quarterly, with additional meetings called within 48 hours of any incident that threatens collection objects or Trust buildings. The Committee is responsible for:

- Reviewing and updating the EPP at least annually;
- Scheduling and evaluating two full-scale evacuation drills per fiscal year, one of which shall be unannounced;
- Maintaining a prioritized salvage list for collection objects, reviewed by the Curator of Collections each July;
- Coordinating training for staff and volunteers on emergency procedures, including fire extinguisher use and first aid.

**10.3 Emergency Contacts and Communications**

The EPP includes a current emergency call-down roster, listing staff and key external contacts (fire, police, utilities, and the Trust’s conservator on retainer). The roster is reviewed quarterly by the Facilities Manager. In the event of an emergency, the senior Trust staff member on site shall serve as Incident Commander until the Facilities Manager or Director arrives. All staff are expected to follow the "Personnel Safety First" protocol: no collection object shall be retrieved if doing so places any person at risk.

**10.4 Insurance Program**

The Trust maintains an all-risk fine arts insurance policy, covering collection objects on the Trust’s premises, in transit, and on loan to or from the Trust. The policy is held with Meridian Mutual Insurance Group, policy number MM-FA-2024-1187, effective July 1, 2024, renewable annually. The policy provides wall-to-wall coverage for objects on loan to the Trust, subject to the terms of the applicable loan agreement.

For outgoing loans, the borrowing institution must provide a certificate of insurance naming the Trust as an additional insured, with coverage limits at least equal to the declared value of the loaned objects. The Registrar shall verify that all certificates are current before any object is shipped. For incoming loans, the Trust’s policy provides coverage, but the Registrar shall confirm that the lender’s policy does not contain a subrogation waiver that would impair the Trust’s coverage.

The Director of Administration reviews the insurance program annually with the Trust’s broker, Meridian Risk Advisors, and reports any material changes to the Board of Trustees at its fall meeting.

**10.5 Salvage Priorities**

The salvage priority list, maintained by the Curator of Collections, categorizes collection objects into three tiers:

- **Tier I (highest priority):** Objects of exceptional cultural significance or irreplaceable value, including the Trust’s permanent collection highlights and any objects on loan with a declared value over $250,000.
- **Tier II:** Objects of significant research value or those with active conservation treatment records.
- **Tier III:** Objects that are duplicates, in poor condition, or of limited interpretive value.

1. INTRODUCTION

The Meridian County Heritage Trust (MCHT) presents its Annual Budget and Operational Plan for Fiscal Year 2025 (FY2025), covering the period from 2025-07-01 through 2026-06-30. This document consolidates the institutional budget, departmental allocations, and key operational priorities for the coming year. It serves as the primary financial and planning reference for all MCHT staff, the Board of Trustees, and our funding partners.

This plan reflects the Trust’s continued commitment to responsible stewardship of the county’s cultural heritage, balanced growth of our public programs, and the preservation of our collections for future generations. The budget and operational priorities outlined herein were developed through a collaborative process involving department heads, the Finance Office, and the Board’s Finance Committee, with final adoption occurring at the regular Board meeting on 2025-04-10.

2. TOTAL ANNUAL BUDGET

The Meridian County Heritage Trust annual_budget for the current fiscal year is 1250000 USD. Record status: current. This figure represents a 4.2% increase over the FY2024 adopted budget of $1,200,000 and reflects additional revenue from increased county appropriations, expanded membership, and a successful capital campaign for the East Wing renovation, completed in late 2024.

This total annual budget is the baseline for all departmental allocations and expenditure plans detailed in Section 3 below. All financial reporting and variance analysis for FY2025 will be measured against this adopted budget figure.

3. DEPARTMENTAL BUDGET ALLOCATIONS

The FY2025 budget is allocated across six major departments and administrative units. Allocations are based on strategic priorities, historical spending patterns, and anticipated needs for the coming year.

| Department / Unit | FY2025 Allocation (USD) | % of Total Budget | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Collections & Conservation | 385,000 | 30.8% | Includes treatment supplies, storage upgrades, and contracted conservator fees |
| Exhibitions & Curatorial | 275,000 | 22.0% | Covers exhibition development, installation, and deinstallation costs |
| Public Programs & Education | 185,000 | 14.8% | Programs, workshops, school group visits, and outreach |
| Facilities & Operations | 210,000 | 16.8% | Building maintenance, utilities, security, and custodial services |
| Development & Membership | 95,000 | 7.6% | Fundraising, membership drives, donor events, and communications |
| Administration & Finance | 100,000 | 8.0% | Salaries for administrative staff, insurance, audit fees, and general office expenses |
| **Total** | **1,250,000** | **100.0%** | |

*Note: Figures are rounded to the nearest whole dollar. The total reflects the adopted annual budget of 1250000 USD.*

3.1 Collections & Conservation

The Collections & Conservation department receives the largest single allocation in FY2025, reflecting the Trust’s recognition that the care and preservation of our collections is the foundation of all our work. Key priorities for this department in FY2025 include:

- **Conservation Treatments:** Contracted conservators will complete treatment of three major works from the permanent collection, including the 19th-century landscape painting “River Bend at Dusk” and two early 20th-century works on paper. A total of $45,000 is budgeted for contracted conservation services.
- **Storage Upgrades:** The completion of the East Wing renovation allows for the rehousing of approximately 2,000 objects from off-site storage into the new climate-controlled storage space. An allocation of $60,000 covers new shelving, archival boxes, and environmental monitoring equipment.
- **Preventive Conservation Supplies:** Ongoing supplies for integrated pest management, housekeeping, and environmental monitoring are budgeted at $15,000.
- **Emergency Preparedness:** An allocation of $10,000 supports the purchase of additional emergency response supplies, including salvage kits and backup generators for climate control systems.

**5.3 Curatorial Staffing**

The Curatorial Department is led by the Chief Curator and includes three full-time Curators (American History, Natural History, and Textiles & Costume), one full-time Assistant Curator, and one full-time Exhibitions Preparator. Curators are responsible for research, exhibition development, and interpretation of the permanent collections. The Exhibitions Preparator manages the fabrication, installation, and maintenance of exhibition components.

Curatorial staff are expected to support public programs by delivering occasional gallery talks and participating in community outreach events. No changes to curatorial staffing are proposed for FY2025.

**5.4 Public Programs & Education Staffing**

The Public Programs & Education Department is managed by the Director of Public Programs & Education. The department includes two full-time Education Coordinators, two full-time Museum Educators, one full-time School Programs Liaison, and one full-time Visitor Services Supervisor (counted under Front-of-House in Section 5.1). The department also employs part-time program facilitators on an as-needed basis for workshops, summer camps, and evening events.

**5.5 Facilities & Operations Staffing**

The Facilities & Operations Department is supervised by the Facilities Manager. The department employs two full-time Maintenance Technicians, one full-time Custodian, one full-time Security Supervisor, and one full-time Security Officer. Part-time security officers are contracted to cover overnight patrols and weekend shifts, totaling 1.0 FTE.

The Facilities Manager oversees the maintenance of the museum’s two buildings, the main museum facility and the off-site collections storage annex. Routine maintenance, janitorial services, and groundskeeping are performed by in-house staff. Major capital repairs and system replacements are contracted externally and are budgeted under the Capital Reserve Fund described in Section 6.

**5.6 Development & Membership Staffing**

The Development & Membership Department is led by the Director of Development. The department includes one full-time Membership Coordinator, one full-time Grants Writer, and one full-time Development Coordinator. The new Development Coordinator position, added in FY2025, will focus on individual giving and annual fundraising campaigns.

The department manages the museum’s membership program, annual fundraising events, and grant reporting. In FY2025, the department will launch a new planned-giving initiative targeting long-time members and local estate planners.

**5.7 Volunteers and Interns**

Volunteers are an integral part of museum operations. In FY2024, 87 active volunteers contributed approximately 6,200 hours of service across all departments. Volunteers serve as gallery hosts, research library assistants, archival processing aides, and event support staff. The Volunteer Coordinator, a part-time position funded through the Public Programs & Education budget, recruits, trains, and schedules volunteers.

Internships are offered on a semester basis in the Collections & Conservation, Curatorial, and Public Programs & Education departments. Internships are unpaid and may be completed for academic credit at the student’s institution. Interns are supervised by a full-time staff member in their assigned department.

**5.8 Personnel Policies**

The Trust maintains personnel policies that apply to all full-time and part-time employees, as detailed in the Employee Handbook (revised January 2024). Key policies include:

- All employees are subject to a background check prior to employment.

**6.1 Collections Stewardship Policy Overview**

The Meridian County Heritage Trust (MCHT) is committed to the responsible stewardship of the collections held in the public trust. This Section establishes the operational framework for the care, documentation, access, and preservation of all objects, specimens, and archival materials in the permanent collection, as well as long-term loans. The policy is reviewed annually by the Collections Committee and the Board of Trustees.

The stewardship program is guided by the following core principles:

- **Preventive Conservation:** Maintaining stable environmental conditions and implementing integrated pest management to prevent damage.
- **Documentation:** Maintaining accurate, complete, and accessible records for every object, from acquisition through deaccession.
- **Access:** Balancing public and scholarly access with the long-term preservation needs of the collection.
- **Professional Standards:** Adhering to the codes of ethics and best practices established by the American Alliance of Museums and the American Institute for Conservation.

**6.2 Collections Committee**

The Collections Committee is a standing committee of the Board of Trustees responsible for reviewing and making recommendations on acquisitions, deaccessions, loans, and other collection-related matters. The Committee meets at least quarterly and as needed for urgent matters.

The Committee's duties are defined in the MCHT Bylaws, Article VII, and include:

1. Reviewing and recommending to the Board all proposed acquisitions and deaccessions.
2. Approving all incoming and outgoing loans in accordance with the Loan Policy.
3. Reviewing the annual Collections Care and Conservation Plan.
4. Recommending updates to collection-related policies for Board approval.
5. Reviewing the status of the Collections Assessment for Preservation program.

**6.3 Acquisition and Deaccession Procedures**

**6.3.1 Acquisitions**

All proposed acquisitions, whether by gift, purchase, bequest, or transfer, must be reviewed by the Collections Committee. The following documentation must be submitted to the Committee for each proposed acquisition:

- **Proposal Form (Form C-101):** Completed by the Curator of the relevant discipline, including the proposed method of acquisition, estimated value, and proposed source of funding.
- **Condition Report (Form C-102):** Prepared by the Registrar or Conservation Department, documenting the physical condition of the object.
- **Provenance Documentation:** All available documentation establishing the chain of custody and legal title. The museum will not acquire objects with uncertain or incomplete provenance.
- **TEFAF Guidelines:** For any object with a possible Holocaust-era provenance gap, the museum will follow the TEFAF Guidelines for the examination of such works.

### 7. Facilities Management

#### 7.1 Overview

The Meridian County Heritage Trust maintains three principal facilities: the Main Museum Building (constructed 1928, renovated 1998), the East Annex Storage Facility (constructed 1985, climate-controlled 2012), and the Carriage House Education Center (constructed 1904, restored 2007). This section establishes operational procedures, maintenance schedules, and budget allocations for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2024.

#### 7.2 Work Order System

All maintenance and repair requests shall be submitted through the Facilities Work Order System (FWOS). The system is administered by the Facilities Manager and is accessible to all department heads and authorized staff.

**Work Order Priority Levels:**

| Priority | Definition | Response Time | Completion Target |
|----------|------------|---------------|-------------------|
| P1 | Imminent threat to life, safety, or collections | Immediate | Within 24 hours |
| P2 | Significant disruption to operations or potential collections risk | Within 4 hours | Within 5 business days |
| P3 | Routine maintenance or minor repairs | Within 2 business days | Within 15 business days |
| P4 | Deferred or cosmetic work | Scheduled | Per maintenance calendar |

**Work Order Lifecycle:**

1. **Submission:** Requester completes Form F-201 (Work Order Request) via the FWOS portal or paper form at the Facilities Office.
2. **Triage:** Facilities Manager reviews and assigns priority level within one business day.
3. **Assignment:** Work is assigned to in-house staff or external contractor as appropriate.
4. **Execution:** Work is performed in accordance with applicable safety and museum standards.
5. **Documentation:** Completed work orders are closed with a record of actions taken, materials used, and hours billed.
6. **Review:** Monthly review of open and closed work orders by the Facilities Manager and Director of Operations.

All work orders involving collections spaces (galleries, storage, conservation labs) require notification to the Registrar prior to commencement of work.

#### 7.5 Conservation and Treatment Protocols

The Conservation Department operates under the supervision of the Chief Conservator and in accordance with the MCHT Collections Management Policy and the Code of Ethics of the American Institute for Conservation. All conservation work, whether performed in-house or by approved external contractors, shall be planned, documented, and reviewed as set forth in this Section.

**7.5.1 Treatment Authorization Levels**

The following authorization levels shall apply to all conservation treatments, including examination, preventive conservation, and interventive treatment:

| Level | Description | Authorizing Authority |
|-------|-------------|----------------------|
| Level I | Examination and documentation only; no physical alteration | Conservator (staff) |
| Level II | Low-risk preventive conservation (e.g., rehousing, mounting, surface cleaning with documented low risk) | Conservator with notice to Registrar |
| Level III | Interventive treatment with minimal risk (e.g., consolidation, inpainting, lining) | Chief Conservator |
| Level IV | Major or high-risk treatment (e.g., structural treatment, extensive loss compensation, treatment of objects on loan) | Chief Conservator and Registrar; Director of Collections notified |
| Level V | Emergency stabilization of an object in imminent danger | Senior Conservator on call; retrospective approval by Chief Conservator within five (5) business days |

No treatment shall begin without a written condition assessment and a signed treatment proposal. For Level III and above, the written proposal must include a justification of the proposed materials and methods, a risk assessment, and a projected schedule and cost estimate. The Registrar shall be notified of all Level III and above treatments prior to commencement.

**7.5.2 Condition Assessments and Treatment Documentation**

A condition assessment shall be completed for every object before it is considered for loan, before it is placed on permanent or temporary display, and upon its return from a loan or exhibition. Assessments shall be recorded on the standard MCHT Condition Report form (Form CR-1) and shall include a written description of the object's condition, a photographic record, and a sketch or diagram where appropriate. A copy of each condition report shall be filed in the object's permanent record in the Collections Management System (CMS) and the original filed with the Registrar.

Treatment documentation shall include the following:

1. **Treatment Proposal:** A written plan of the proposed treatment, including materials, methods, and a schedule.
2. **Treatment Record:** A written narrative of the treatment actually performed, including materials used, methods employed, and any deviations from the proposal.
3. **Photographic Documentation:** Before, during, and after photographs of the treatment, taken under standard lighting conditions and filed with the treatment record.
4. **Final Report:** A summary of the treatment, including an assessment of the outcome and any recommendations for future care.

All treatment documentation shall be reviewed by the Chief Conservator and filed in the object's permanent record.

**7.5.3 Conservation Laboratory Access and Use**

The Conservation Lab shall be accessible only to authorized Conservation Department staff and approved interns, fellows, and contractors. Access to the lab shall be controlled by the Security Department and recorded in the lab access log. All lab users shall complete a safety orientation before working in the lab. Use of lab equipment shall be in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and the lab's standard operating procedures. The Chief Conservator shall maintain an inventory of lab equipment and hazardous materials, and shall review the inventory quarterly.

**8.0 PHOTOGRAPHY AND DOCUMENTATION STANDARDS**

**8.1 Purpose**

This section establishes uniform standards for the creation, handling, and storage of photographic and audiovisual documentation produced by or on behalf of the Trust. These standards apply to all staff, volunteers, interns, fellows, contractors, and visiting researchers. The goal is to ensure that all visual records are accurate, reproducible, and securely preserved as part of the Trust’s permanent institutional memory.

**8.2 Photography Studio Operations**

The Photography Studio, located in the lower level of the Heritage Center (Room B-14), is the primary facility for all controlled photographic work on collection objects. The Studio is equipped with copy stands, light tents, strobes, and a calibrated EIZO monitor for color review. The Studio is scheduled through the Collections Department’s shared calendar; all shoots must be booked at least 48 hours in advance, except for emergency documentation required by the Registrar or Chief Conservator.

Studio access is restricted to authorized staff and approved contractors. A log of all studio sessions shall be maintained by the Photographer, recording the date, object accession number, photographer’s initials, and purpose of the shoot. The log is reviewed monthly by the Registrar.

**8.3 Photography Survey Logs**

The Trust maintains a series of survey logs to track photographic coverage of the permanent collection. The primary log, the **Photography Survey Log (Form PS-1)**, is a master index of all objects photographed since the 1987 inventory. Each entry includes the accession number, object name, date of photography, photographer’s initials, and the location of the digital files. The log is updated within five working days of any new shoot.

A second log, the **Survey Completion Log (Form PS-2)**, tracks the progress of the ongoing effort to photograph the entire collection. As of the start of FY2025, the Trust has complete photographic coverage of 8,412 of the 9,108 objects in the permanent collection. The remaining 696 objects are scheduled for photography over the next two fiscal years, with priority given to objects on loan, objects slated for exhibition, and objects in the Archaeology Collection that have not been photographed since 1995.

**8.4 Digital File Standards**

All born-digital images shall be captured in RAW format and archived as uncompressed TIFF masters. Delivery files for web and publication use shall be JPEG or PNG, generated from the master file. The following naming convention shall be used for all digital files:

*Accession Number_Object Name_View_Date_Photographer Initials*

Example: `1987.004.002_Basin_Overall_20240910_JAB.tif`

All master files shall be stored on the Trust’s network-attached storage (NAS) in the folder structure maintained by the IT Department. A second copy shall be stored on the off-site backup server, which is tested quarterly by IT. No master files shall be stored solely on local drives or removable media.

**8.5 Rights and Reproduction**

The Trust retains all rights to images produced by its staff and contractors during the course of their work. Images of collection objects may be used for internal documentation, conservation, research, and educational purposes without further approval. Any external use, including publication, exhibition, or commercial licensing, requires written approval from the Registrar and, where applicable, the donor or lender.

**Section 9: Collections Management**

**9.1 Scope and Authority**

This section governs the day-to-day care, documentation, movement, and use of the permanent collection and any objects on loan to the Trust. The Registrar is the designated authority for all matters concerning object location, custody, and legal status. Department heads shall ensure that all staff and volunteers under their supervision are familiar with the policies in this section.

**9.2 Accessioning and Deaccessioning**

The Trust shall accession objects into the permanent collection only through the procedures outlined in the Collections Management Policy, approved by the Board of Trustees. No object shall be formally accessioned without a fully executed deed of gift or purchase invoice, a signed receipt from the Registrar, and a preliminary condition report.

Deaccessioning of any object shall follow the same policy, which requires a written recommendation from the Curator of Collections, review by the Collections Committee, and final approval by the Board of Trustees. All deaccession proceeds shall be used exclusively for the acquisition or conservation of collection objects. No deaccession shall occur for the purpose of raising operating funds.

**9.3 Loan Management**

All incoming and outgoing loans shall be administered through the Registrar’s Office. No loan shall be accepted or initiated without a fully executed loan agreement approved by the Registrar and, for outgoing loans, the Director.

| Loan Type | Approval Authority | Agreement Required | Insurance Responsibility |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Incoming (short-term, under 1 year) | Registrar | Yes – Standard Incoming Loan Agreement | Lender, unless otherwise specified |
| Incoming (long-term, 1 year or more) | Director | Yes – Extended Loan Agreement | Trust, at replacement value |
| Outgoing | Director and Curator of Collections | Yes – Standard Outgoing Loan Agreement | Borrowing institution, wall-to-wall |
| Internal (between Trust buildings) | Registrar | No – Internal Movement Form (Form CM-4) | N/A |

The Registrar shall maintain a central loan file for each active loan, containing the signed agreement, condition reports, insurance certificates, correspondence, and a copy of the courier report (if applicable). Loan files shall be reviewed annually for renewal or termination status.

For outgoing loans, the borrowing institution must provide a facilities report that meets the Trust’s environmental and security standards. The Registrar shall verify that the borrower’s insurance certificate names the Trust as an additional insured. A condition report shall be completed by a Trust staff member before shipment and again upon the object’s return.

**9.4 Location Control and Movement**

The Registrar maintains the central location index for all collection objects. Any change in an object’s location shall be reported to the Registrar’s Office within two working days. Departmental staff are responsible for updating the location field in the collections database (TMS) when they move an object within their assigned storage or exhibition areas.

All movement of collection objects within the Trust’s buildings shall be performed by trained staff or authorized volunteers. Objects shall be transported on padded carts or in appropriate crates, and no object shall be left unattended in a corridor or common area.

**9.5 Object Handling**

Only staff who have completed the Trust’s Object Handling Training shall handle collection objects. The training is coordinated by the Curator of Collections and is offered quarterly. A roster of trained staff is maintained by the Registrar’s Office.

**SECTION 10. EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS AND COLLECTION RISK MANAGEMENT**

**10.1 Policy Statement**

The Trust maintains a comprehensive Emergency Preparedness Plan (EPP), current as of March 2024, which addresses fire, flood, severe weather, utility failure, and security incidents affecting any Trust-owned or Trust-operated facility. The EPP is a living document, reviewed annually by the Emergency Preparedness Committee and updated whenever a drill, incident, or facilities assessment identifies a gap. The plan is distributed to all department heads, the Facilities Manager, and the Registrar’s Office; a copy is kept in the Security Office and in the Director’s office.

**10.2 Emergency Preparedness Committee**

The Committee is chaired by the Facilities Manager and includes the Curator of Collections, the Registrar, the Head of Security, and the Director of Administration. The Committee meets quarterly, with additional meetings called within 48 hours of any incident that threatens collection objects or Trust buildings. The Committee is responsible for:

- Reviewing and updating the EPP at least annually;
- Scheduling and evaluating two full-scale evacuation drills per fiscal year, one of which shall be unannounced;
- Maintaining a prioritized salvage list for collection objects, reviewed by the Curator of Collections each July;
- Coordinating training for staff and volunteers on emergency procedures, including fire extinguisher use and first aid.

**10.3 Emergency Contacts and Communications**

The EPP includes a current emergency call-down roster, listing staff and key external contacts (fire, police, utilities, and the Trust’s conservator on retainer). The roster is reviewed quarterly by the Facilities Manager. In the event of an emergency, the senior Trust staff member on site shall serve as Incident Commander until the Facilities Manager or Director arrives. All staff are expected to follow the "Personnel Safety First" protocol: no collection object shall be retrieved if doing so places any person at risk.

**10.4 Insurance Program**

The Trust maintains an all-risk fine arts insurance policy, covering collection objects on the Trust’s premises, in transit, and on loan to or from the Trust. The policy is held with Meridian Mutual Insurance Group, policy number MM-FA-2024-1187, effective July 1, 2024, renewable annually. The policy provides wall-to-wall coverage for objects on loan to the Trust, subject to the terms of the applicable loan agreement.

For outgoing loans, the borrowing institution must provide a certificate of insurance naming the Trust as an additional insured, with coverage limits at least equal to the declared value of the loaned objects. The Registrar shall verify that all certificates are current before any object is shipped. For incoming loans, the Trust’s policy provides coverage, but the Registrar shall confirm that the lender’s policy does not contain a subrogation waiver that would impair the Trust’s coverage.

The Director of Administration reviews the insurance program annually with the Trust’s broker, Meridian Risk Advisors, and reports any material changes to the Board of Trustees at its fall meeting.

**10.5 Salvage Priorities**

The salvage priority list, maintained by the Curator of Collections, categorizes collection objects into three tiers:

- **Tier I (highest priority):** Objects of exceptional cultural significance or irreplaceable value, including the Trust’s permanent collection highlights and any objects on loan with a declared value over $250,000.
- **Tier II:** Objects of significant research value or those with active conservation treatment records.
- **Tier III:** Objects that are duplicates, in poor condition, or of limited interpretive value.
